_comment: Sound design for the revised chapter 5. Built from assets that already
exist, so it cost no ElevenLabs credits.
THE QUIET EVENT STILL GOVERNS: local machinery and the world outside, never
a settlement alarm. Nobody sounds a siren in these chapters.
Levels are DERIVED from audio/config.json's categoryTargetLufs and each
asset's measured loudness. `emphasisDb` is the only hand-set number, and in
this movement it is mostly one sound: the deep distant vibration, which
gets louder every time it returns.

cues.why: The control room again, and it STOPS when Jack gets into the vehicle. A bed that followed him outdoors would say the room came with him, which is exactly the thing this chapter is about not being true any more.
'He opened the settlement broadcast controls.' The same intercom the lab uses, because it is the settlement's own system -- and it is the first time in the story anyone addresses the whole town.
'Then he pressed transmit.' One small tone under the last word of the beat, so the announcement begins on a machine rather than on a breath.
'Jack ended the broadcast.' The silence after it is doing the work, so nothing else sounds here.
'A call indicator appeared on Jack's console.' Lena, from the emergency coordination channel.
Held open through the water estimate and the vibration map, closing on the knock at the door -- which is where Lena stops being a voice and walks in.

'Then the building vibrated again.' It arrives on the one light moment in the movement, mid-laugh, and takes it away. Carried over at Chapter 4's loudest level because it is the same thing, no nearer yet.
The control-room door opening for Lena and the two officers. The knock itself has no asset and is left to the prose; what is heard is the door, which is the part that changes the room.
Jack checking the southern boundary feeds before agreeing to go.

THE FIRST TIME THE STORY GOES OUTSIDE AT THE NEW SCALE, and it uses the night ambience Joshua supplied. It has to be quiet and ordinary -- crickets, air, a night like any other -- because the horror of the scene is that it SOUNDS normal while a blade of grass stands over a man. Runs to the end of the chapter, through the drive back.
The environmental sensor taking its first reading at the boundary. Six dB under the other terminal chirps: outdoors, in the open, a small instrument in one hand.
Jack zooming the wrist camera onto the pale object. Quiet, because the next sound in the scene should be nothing at all -- 'Nobody spoke for several seconds' is four beats away.

'A vibration rolled through the ground.' The loudest in the movement so far, +7 dB, and the first one heard from OUTSIDE a building rather than through a floor. This is the moment the thing stops being a report.

'The vehicle accelerated away from the boundary.' A low body of sound under the line rather than an engine, which the library does not have. Eight dB down: it is a departure, not an event, and the chapter's last line belongs to the grass still moving behind them.
